#### Image

Runs use an image the application builds itself, with `podman build`, and keeps up to date: the default image, holding the harness commands, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode, and piton, each at the version installed on the host where it can be found there, and at its latest otherwise. It is built again when any of those versions changes.
Each command the image holds has to run in it, not only be there. The build ends by running each one's version command in the image, as `piton --version`, and a build where one fails, as a piton built against a newer C library than the image has, fails, saying which command couldn't run and what it printed. An image whose piton can't run is never used, so a Spec run is never sent where it can't run `piton build` to check its work.
A project can add to it with a Containerfile of its own, `.suspense/Containerfile`, built FROM the default image, to add what its runs in a container need, as the [ProjectDataScope](../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says. The project's image is built from it, and kept, and built again only when the Containerfile or the default image changes. Without one, the project's runs use the default image.
While an image is being built for a run, the task or question shows "Preparing environment" as its status, and what the build prints goes to its raw output. A build that fails fails the run, saying why.
The image is a Linux image, whatever the host is, so what it holds is installed in it for Linux, for the architecture Podman runs: each harness and piton at the version found on the host, from its own Linux release or package, never a binary copied from the host, which on macOS or Windows can't run in it. The build is given only the Containerfile the application writes for it, in a build context of its own, a fresh temporary directory holding nothing else, never the project or the user's home, and needs nothing from the host but the network. A version that can't be found on the host, or isn't published for Linux, is installed at its latest.
Only one build of an image runs at a time. A run, a login, or a welcome or settings check that needs an image already being built waits for that build and shares how it ended, rather than starting another, so two builds never race to tag the same image. A build is tagged only once it has succeeded, so a build that fails or is interrupted never leaves an image that is taken for a good one, and the next need of it builds it again.
A build that fails says why in Podman's own words: the step it failed at and everything the build printed, as written, never only that the image couldn't be created, and the same is kept in the log the application writes for its builds, beside its preferences.

#### Mounts

What each run sees is what is mounted into its container, and nothing else from the host. The project is mounted at the same fixed path in the container, `/workspace`, on every platform, each location given at its place relative to the project directory under `/workspace`, and the run works in `/workspace`. So a harness that keys its sessions on its working directory, as Claude Code does, finds them again after the project moves, whatever its path on the host. What each kind of run is given, as the [ProjectLocationsScope](../project-locations/index.md#project-locations-scope) names the locations, follows.

##### Spec

A Spec task, or a Chain prompt's spec step or spec follow-up: the spec location, read and write; the compiled reference, the harness directory's reference folder, read and write, so it can run `piton build` itself; the project's `.piton` directory, which holds the build's manifest of the files it owns, read and write, for the same reason, bound in from the project itself, never an empty, temporary, or copied one, so the manifest a build in the container starts from is the host's, and what it writes there is the host's next build's, the application creating the directory in the project first where it isn't there; the Suspense fluency file, read only; the fluency file, read only; piton.config.pi, read only; and the task's understanding file, read and write. Never the code location: in its place, an empty scratch directory, writable, that nothing else sees and that goes with the container, so `piton build` finds the code location it places the shape's guidance in.

##### Question

A question from the Ask tab: the code location, the spec location, the compiled reference, and piton.config.pi, each read only, so it can run `piton slice` in its container, and the Suspense fluency file, read only. Nothing is writable but the harness's own volume and the questions' sessions folder. Where one of the code location and the spec location holds the other, both are still mounted, read only, and neither is hidden from the question by the other.

Each run is also given its own conversation's sessions folder, read and write, as Volumes says, and nothing of any other conversation's.
Nothing else is ever mounted: not the user's home directory, the user's own skills, MCP servers, or user-level CLAUDE.md, and not the project's git directory. A location that holds another, as a code location holding the spec or the project data, is mounted without the one it holds, so the one held is never seen through it, unless the run is given the one held as well, as a question is given both the code location and the spec location.
A task's understanding file is mounted on its own, never the history folder it is in, so a run sees no other task's record. Since a file has to be there to be mounted, the application writes it empty just before the run, and an empty understanding file is shown as one not written yet is.

#### Paths

On every platform, every path a run reports from its container is mapped back to its host path, `/workspace` standing for the project directory, before it is shown or opened anywhere: the referenced spec in the right sidebar, file links in the task's output, its understanding file, the files it changed, and what its tool calls touched. Only a path that is `/workspace`, or begins with `/workspace/`, is mapped, never text that merely holds it, as `/workspace-old`. A path that maps to nothing on the host is shown as the run gave it, and opens nothing.

content.text:
I couldn't reproduce your exact error without its text, but one likely cause is now fixed, along with the other spec gaps. All 529 tests pass. I haven't done a full `podman build` and first login here; that downloads the Node image and installs every harness.

**Likeliest cause:** on Linux, the image build copied your host's `piton` binary into the Debian image. Yours is built with cargo, so if it needs a newer C library than the image has, it fails the build's "can it run?" check. That fails the whole image, and with it the first login. On macOS and Windows the image had no piton at all.

What changed in `src/container.rs`:
- **piton:**
  - It's installed from piton's own Linux release with its `install.sh`, at your host's version, or the latest release if that version isn't published. Your 0.1.59 isn't, so it falls back to 0.1.58; I ran that step for real.
  - Linux builds exist only for x86-64, so on an arm64 Podman machine (Apple Silicon) the image goes without piton, and the check allows that. A piton that's present but won't run still fails the build.
  - `curl` is added to the image for this.
- **Build:**
  - The build context is a fresh folder holding only the Containerfile.
  - Only one build of an image runs at a time; a run or login that needs one already building waits for it and gets the same result.
  - The image is tagged only after its commands pass the check, so a failed or interrupted build never leaves an image that looks good.
- **Errors:** a failed build now says the step it failed at plus Podman's last 40 lines, where it used to say only "podman failed" and the last line. The full output is appended to `image-builds.log` beside the preferences.
- **Volume:** the harness's volume is created with `podman volume create --ignore` before the first login or status check. It's still mounted with `:U`, so it's owned by the user the container runs as.

**Login view** (`src/login_view.rs`): it builds the image first, showing "Preparing environment…" and the build output. If the build fails, it shows why in red with a **Try again** button and starts no login. Login failures are reported as before.

**Where the spec and the code differ:** the spec gives `~/.claude` as where the volume sits beneath HOME. The code mounts it at HOME itself, owned by the container's user. I left that as it is, because Claude Code also keeps its login in `~/.claude.json` at HOME's top level, and a volume at `~/.claude` alone would log you out after every run.

If it still fails, the login view now shows the step and Podman's output, and `image-builds.log` has the whole build. Send me either and I can pin down the cause.
